newsitem.title: ESTONIA: TALLINN MAYOR APPOINTED NEW INTERIOR MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: TALLINN MAYOR APPOINTED NEW INTERIOR MINISTER.

text.p: President Lennart Meri on Wednesday approved the mayor of Tallinn, Robert Lepikson, as new interior minister.
The president's office said in a statement that Lepikson was named as the new member of the government.

"I presented Lepikson as an active person who generates ideas and makes them happen, who has actively led Tallinn as well as in his work as a permanent head of the defence ministry," Prime Minister Mart Siimann told a news conference.
Former interior minister Riivo Sinijarv was dismissed yesterday at the request of Siimann and is to move into diplomatic work.
No reason was given but local news agencies said the premier was unhappy at the way Sinijarv handled an investigation into the abuse of official cars by ministry officials.
"Lepikson is expected to be sworn in before the Riigikogu (parliament) on Monday, May 5, before he can take up his new duties," Siimann said.
Lepikson, 45, is also a deputy leader of Siimann's Coalition Party. He was educated as an engineer and was recently permanent under-secretary at the defence ministry.
Before his appointment to the defence ministry, he was the director of the Estonian metal export company, EMEX. He was appointed to the board of Uhispank in early April.
Siimann said that Sinijarv was more suitable to diplomatic work than in a ministry where there were lots of "complicated tensions".
Siimann said the decision on a new mayor for Tallinn was up to the city government.
